thread.title: Sonos Is Undervalued At 1x Forward Sales With 14% Y/Y Revenue Growth - Sonos, Inc. (NASDAQ:SONO)

author: Wilsonville Capital
title: Sonos Is Undervalued At 1x Forward Sales With 14% Y/Y Revenue Growth - Sonos, Inc. (NASDAQ:SONO)
text:
Exhibiting revenue growth of 14% y/y and having agreements with large retailers like IKEA, Sonos (NASDAQ: SONO ) should be trading at more than 1x forward sales. Other competitors are trading at a higher valuation. In addition, the company reports positive cash flow from operations, and its adjusted EBITDA is expected to grow at 20-27% in the next year. The company seems undervalued by the market.
(Source: 10-Q )
Business And Market Opportunity Founded in 2000 and headquartered in Santa Barbara, California, Sonos sells wireless multi-room home audio and a proprietary software platform. With over 630 issued patents, agreements with about 100 streaming content providers, such as Apple Music ( AAPL ), Pandora ( P ), and Spotify ( SPOT ), Sonos seems a company to be studied very closely.
(Source: Company Prospectus )
The market opportunity is growing at a high pace and is large. Futuresource estimates that there were 50 million new subscribers in 2017. The total amount of subscribers is equal to 175 million, which seems to represent approximately 50% of the total global music market in 2017. The growth in the United States is also remarkable. According to Nielsen, the average number of hours spent listening to music per week increased by 37% in two years to over 32 hours in 2017. The image below provides further details on this matter:
(Source: Nielsen )
Revenue Growth - Sonos Beam The new quarterly report was very beneficial in terms of revenue growth. The company reported $24.34 million more than expected, and 13% more than that in the same quarter in 2017. The revenues for the fiscal year ended September 29, 2018, were at $1.137 billion, a 14% increase as compared to that in 2017. The image below provides further details on this matter:
(Source: Company 8-K )
Sonos explained the good results by noting that Sonos Beam, which was launched in mid-July, has exceeded what the company expected. In addition, it seems to have become the market leader in the soundbar market in the United States. The images below provide further details on this matter.
(Source: Company 8-K)
(Source: Company 8-K)
As explained on the company website, Sonos Beam is a smart speaker permitting users to play music or films and interact with Amazon ( AMZN ) Alexa, Spotify, TuneIn, or Audible. The image below provides further details on this new, innovative device:
(Source: Company Website )
Gross Profit Margin And Net Income Declined With revenues growing at a high pace, investors may not appreciate that the company’s net income and gross profit margin don’t show growth. The issue seems to be in the cost of revenues. Sonos saw how the costs of certain components increased, driving down profitability at the gross profit level. The lines below provide further details on this matter:
(Source: Company 8-K)
The company released a gross profit of $489 million in the year ended September 29, 2018, which shows only a 7% y/y increase. It noted that the release of Sonos One and Beam is also responsible for the decrease in gross profit margin. Read the following lines:
(Source: Company 8-K)
The net loss for the year ended September 29, 2018, was equal to $15.6 million, a bit less than what was reported in 2017. Growth investors may not care about net income losses. For them, the revenue growth and gross profit margins are the most relevant. With that, it is not beneficial that the company is seeing a decline in its net income. The income statement is shown in the image below:
(Source: Company 8-K)
46% y/y Increase In The Amount Of Assets In September 2018, Sonos' balance sheet reported shows a beneficial 69% y/y increase in the amount of cash, amounting to $220 million, and a 46% y/y increase in the amount of assets. Shareholders should appreciate these figures. With that, inventories increased by 69% to $193 million, which certain investors may not appreciate. Let’s expect that the company is able to sell these inventories soon. The image below provides further details on the amount of assets:
(Source: Company 8-K)
With an asset/liability ratio of 1.54x, the liabilities of the company should not worry investors. In addition, the amount of financial debt did not increase in 2018, which investors should appreciate. The amount of accounts payable increased by 71%, amounting to $195 million, which shows that suppliers trust the company. Sonos does not need to obtain debt to pay them, which seems another beneficial feature. The image below provides additional details on its list of liabilities:
(Source: Company 8-K)
Growing EBITDA, Positive Cash Flow from Operations And Partnership With IKEA DCF modelers may appreciate the company. The cash flow from operations reported for the year ended September 30, 2017 and 2018 was positive and equal to $63.9 million and $30.5 million respectively. Take a look at this in the image below:
(Source: Company 8-K)
Additionally, both the adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin were positive in 2018. The adjusted EBITDA grew by 23% y/y, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin increased from 5.6% to 6.1%. The image below provides further details:
(Source: Company 8-K)
With that, it is quite beneficial that Sonos expects 20-27% adjusted EBITDA in 2019. The company noted in the earnings call that it expects to have adjusted EBITDA of $83-88 million. The lines below provide further details on this matter, as well as the expected revenue:
(Source: Sonos Q4 2018 earnings call transcript , Seeking Alpha)
Investors should be wondering whether the company will be able to maintain the same revenue and EBITDA growth in the future. In this regard, it is relevant noting that Sonos has signed agreements with large retailers like IKEA and Amazon. These large and well-known groups should help the company offer its products to consumers. In this regard, read the following lines from the earnings call:
(Source: Sonos Q4 2018 earnings call transcript, Seeking Alpha)
Valuation As of November 18, 2018, with 98.384 million shares outstanding at $15.44 per share, the market capitalization of Sonos is $1.519 billion. Subtracting $220 million in cash and adding $39 million in debt, the enterprise value equals $1.338 billion. Assuming forward revenues of $1.25 billion, the company trades at 1x forward sales. In addition, with adjusted forward EBITDA of $83 million, it trades at 16x forward EBITDA.
The prospectus notes that Sonos competes with the following companies:
Bang & Olufsen ( OTCPK:BGOUF ) Bose Samsung ( OTC:SSNLF ) Sony ( SNE ) Sound United With the exception of Bang & Olufsen, most of these competitors are too large to be compared with Sonos. Bang & Olufsen trades at 1.65x sales and 15.91x EBITDA, with revenue growth of 18.81% and gross profit margin of 34.90%.
Sonos seems undervalued as compared to Bang & Olufsen, not only because it trades at a lower Enterprise Value/Revenues ratio, but also because Sonos is a younger company. Bang & Olufsen was founded in 1925, while Sonos was founded in 2000. Investors expect larger business growth from young companies than older entities. With this in mind, Sonos should trade at more than 1.65x forward sales.
Conclusion With revenue growth of 14% y/y and agreements with large corporations like Ikea, Amazon, and Pandora, Sonos, Inc. should trade at more than 1x forward sales. Competitors like Bang & Olufsen are trading at 1.65x, and they may not grow as much as Sonos. Keep in mind that Sonos is a younger competitor, thus its business model should stay for a longer amount of time. Sonos also shows positive cash flow from operations, and its adjusted EBITDA is expected to grow at 20-27% in the next year. The market does not seem to be recognizing this fact.
